Customer - acme-infra: hey team, streaming from your /v1/stream endpoint keeps dropping for us after ~60s. partial events arrive, then connection closes. we tried reconnecting but client sees truncated output and sometimes 502 from ALB. any ideas?

Maya S: sorry you're hitting this — can you share a simple repro (curl + headers) and whether traffic is going through Cloudflare/ALB/NLB? also include response headers from the failed request if you have them.

Customer - acme-infra: thanks. traffic -> ALB -> nginx origin (behind Cloudflare). repro is: 
```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" "https://api.acme.example/v1/stream?prompt=hello" 
```
we get streaming for ~50-70s, then connection closes with no more bytes. response headers (last request):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
connection: keep-alive
server: envoy
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC


```

Alex C: thanks, that pattern matches idle-timeout/proxy-buffering issues. ALB default idle timeout is 60s — if there’s a period with no bytes flushed across the LB it can close TCP. nginx/proxies can buffer server output and only flush occasionally, which looks like silence to the LB.

Shawn W: can you paste the nginx/upstream config? also which runtime (gunicorn/uvicorn/node/golang) is serving the stream? some runtimes buffer until a flush.

Customer - acme-infra: origin is node (express) using res.write for SSE, we think we flush after every event but not 100% sure. nginx conf snippet (redacted):
```
proxy_buffering on;\nproxy_request_buffering on;\nproxy_read_timeout 90s;\nproxy_send_timeout 60s;\nkeepalive_timeout 75s;\n```
we didn't change ALB idle timeout (probably default).

Ingrid R (cloud-ops): quick checklist:
- ALB default idle timeout is 60s (if the connection experiences >60s inactivity ALB will close). increase it to 300s for streaming workloads:
```
aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn <arn> --attributes Key=idletimeout.timeout_seconds,Value=300
```
- NLB is TCP and won't buffer but has different health/timeout semantics
- Cloudflare will buffer some responses at the edge; to verify origin behavior, temporarily bypass CF (grey cloud) or use the origin CNAME. CF Workers/Stream support streaming but the default CDN layer may buffer.

Maya S: also on nginx, set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off;` and `proxy_send_timeout`/`proxy_read_timeout` > LB idle timeout. ensure `transfer-encoding: chunked` and that the app explicitly flushes after `res.write`. Node example: 
```
res.write('data: ' + JSON.stringify(payload) + "\\n\\n");
// if using compression middleware, disable for SSE or call res.flush() if available
res.flush && res.flush();
```

SRE Bot: common error in logs we see: `upstream prematurely closed connection` or `connection reset by peer` around the same time as ALB idletimeout. also sometimes `recv() failed` from nginx when CF closes connection.

Customer - acme-infra: we dug up the origin logs, here's the sequence: 
```
[00:00:00] stream:start id=abcd
[00:00:45] event: chunk 1 flushed
[00:01:05] event: chunk 2 flushed
[00:01:07] tcp: FIN from load-balancer
[00:01:07] node: socket close by peer
```
so we sent something at 65s but LB closed at 67s? timing looks close.

Alex C: that lines up. two levers: (1) increase ALB idle timeout to > the maximum gap between server flushes, (2) make server send periodic SSE heartbeats/comments at <60s intervals to keep bytes flowing, e.g. a `: keepalive` comment every 15s. also turn off buffering on nginx so each event is visible as traffic across the LB.

Shawn W: here's a quick nginx snippet we've used for SSE origins: 
```
location /v1/stream/ {
  proxy_request_buffering off;
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "keep-alive";
  proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;  # for some setups
  proxy_read_timeout 360s;
}
```
If using gzip/compression middleware, disable it for SSE routes — compression causes buffering.

Customer - acme-infra: interesting — we had gzip enabled globally. i'll try disabling compression for the SSE path and add a heartbeat. any advice on client reconnect behavior? we need to resume where we left off (so users don't miss tokens).

Maya S: two approaches: (A) make streams idempotent and include a resume token in events so client can request continuation with ?after=<token>, (B) use SSE `Last-Event-ID` header/resume semantics — server must support that. Typical pattern: include an event id on each SSE event: `id: <cursor>\ndata: {...}\n\n` so client stores last id and on reconnect uses `Last-Event-ID: <id>` to request resume.

Ingrid R (cloud-ops): also, to triage whether CF is the layer causing buffering/truncation:
1) curl origin directly (bypass CF) using origin host / origin port and the same Authorization header;
2) if origin works but CF path fails, we can file a Cloudflare ticket or recommend leveraging Workers for streaming.

Support Bot: created ticket #SUP-4521 and assigned to eng-runtime for follow-up; escalated as P2.

Alex C: actionable plan for customer:
1) temporarily bypass Cloudflare to test origin directly
2) set `proxy_buffering off` and `proxy_request_buffering off` on nginx and restart
3) increase ALB idle timeout to 300s (or at least > max expected gap)
4) implement short SSE heartbeat (comment line or small no-op event) every 10-20s from the app and ensure you call res.flush()/flushHeaders where appropriate
5) disable compression middleware for SSE path
6) add event `id:` and support resume via Last-Event-ID or cursor query param so reconnects can resume gracefully

Customer - acme-infra: we changed gzip, turned off buffering, and added heartbeat at 15s. after testing over the last hour no disconnects. thanks! we'll still increase ALB timeout to be safe.

Shawn W: perfect. follow-ups for us: eng-runtime to add an internal doc template for SSE production hardening (nginx/ALB/CF checklist), and consider adding adaptive heartbeats from the runtime if a model step takes longer.

Alex C: i'll own the doc and a small runbook. assigning ENG-RUNTIME. closing thread after 24h if no regressions — please reopen if issues reappear. :thumbsup:

Support Bot: ticket #SUP-4521 updated: status=assigned, owner=Alex C, priority=P2.
